A fixed rail train type system would not be feasible, for it requires a high trip demand between realtively fixed terminal points to economically justify investment and operating expenditures. The development of rail commuter service depends on many things but would primarily depend on the attractiveness of such a commuter service and its economic viability to private development. There is no freight or rail service to Mitchell Field. The existing C.M. St. P. & P. R.R. passes within 1-1/2 miles west of the Howell Avenue airport entrance road.
The regional land use-transportation plans clearly established that a fixed rail rapid transit system would be inferior to the more flexible and economical bus modified rapid transit system and no further consideration would be given to other forms of rapid transit.
A rubber-tired busing freeway system, however, has the flexibility of origin and destination and would suit any potential increase in ridership.
Without the direct connection of the Airport Spur freeway it would be difficult, if not impossible, to develop effective modified rapid transit service to the airport and surrounding neighborhood.
